name: King of Hearts
timbre: mild, soft-edged older man's voice, slightly pinched and fussy, that strains for gravity and cracks upward when unsure
pitch: light baritone, affects a deeper 'grave' pitch for pronouncements
accent: educated Received Pronunciation, precise and schoolmasterly, over-careful articulation
reference_style: Pompous-procedural: court formulae, reasoning aloud in circles, conditional threats never followed through, 'my dear' to the Queen. Fussy, not cruel; must sound clearly softer and lower-energy than the Queen.

grave_pronouncement.note: ch011-p68 'in a deep voice'; ch012-p03 'in a very grave voice'

flustered.note: voice cracks when challenged; ch012-p57 'in an offended tone'

aside_low.note: ch009-p42 'in a low voice, to the company generally'

voice_evidence.quote: he said in a deep voice
said the King in a very grave voice
Alice heard the King say in a low voice

reason: Deep/grave/low deliveries are sourced; the soft cracking baseline follows personality ('a voice that starts grave and cracks when he is challenged').
